body:
instead of patching in render args, we could also patch in `on('results')` or similar, although when I tried that, that was slightly too late (a "result" render would be able to cause a temporary render with result state instead of eager state).

I'm not the biggest fan of doing this patching here, so if another place makes sense, that would be nice.

It can't be the constructor of search results, as that should still be based on the associated _state, as otherwise we're reading from the wrong query (eg previous query had a disjunctive refinement, current state doesn't have that, you don't want to read from first query, but still from second query, only after results are instantiated you patch _state).
this is part A of the implementation

I don't understand why the bottom assertion fails. It already is the case before this PR actually, as the assertion was written wrong (before this PR it already was checked, now the local state is trusted, and thus not checked).

Because the assertion was originally written wrong, I'm kind of doubting whether https://github.com/algolia/react-instantsearch/issues/3530 was even asserted by this test.

This test was never correctly passing: 

- searchClient wasn't correct (returned no facets on result)
- and behaviour it pretended to fix was never fixed (if result._state said something was refined, it would show as refined, but first click would only set it to refined again, second click would toggle again, because local search parameters are used for `refine`)

And the behaviour changed in this PR. It's sufficiently covered under the expanded "renders refinements from local widget state" test now.
